bullets: Came to the Jets from Indianapolis in the November 2025 trade that sent CB Sauce Gardner to the Colts (Jets also got a 2026 and 2027 first-round pick) — not a 2026 in-season move, but this is his first note on this roster.

Has emerged as the Jets' clear top target earner through two 2026 weeks: 3/3 for 60 yards in Week 1, then a team-high 6 catches on 12 targets for 63 yards in Week 2's OT loss to Green Bay (29.3% of Geno Smith's 41 attempts), while playing 61 of 74 offensive snaps.

Clear volume-driven breakout profile early — production (301 yards in 8 games with NYJ post-trade) already outpacing his limited Indianapolis run (464 yards in 25 games), and he's now commanding target shares that put him firmly in the Jets' WR1/WR2 conversation.

Chicago's veteran (age 34) placekicker with no roster competition — the Bears carry him as their only kicker, and he's signed to a 4-year, ~$16M extension, making his role about as secure as any kicker in the league.

Went 1-for-1 on field goals (40-yarder) plus 8/8 PATs in Week 1's 59-37 win over Carolina (11 total points); in Week 2's low-scoring 9-3 loss at Minnesota he hit a 50-yard FG to tie it 3-3 early, but had a potential game-tying 23-yard attempt blocked by Isaiah Rodgers with 6:21 left — Chicago's offensive struggles (particularly after Caleb Williams' injury exit) capped his ceiling that week.

2025 accuracy dipped to 83% (down from 92% in 2023), a mild efficiency note, but he remains the Bears' all-time leader in 50+ yard field goals and a proven high-floor streaming option, especially in projected shootouts.
Ravens' primary place-kicker heading into Week 1 — a low-variance role, but a full-time job on a good offense.
One of the most accurate kickers in the league since entering the NFL, including elite long-range range — locked in as Dallas' K1 with no competition.
Detroit's starting kicker on one of the league's most efficient offenses — plenty of scoring opportunities behind a strong O-line.
Veteran incumbent, Houston's clear starting kicker with no camp competition reported.
Jacksonville's starting kicker, known for elite leg strength on long attempts — no competition for the job.
Longtime Seahawks starter with no reported competition — steady, low-variance K1 role.
San Francisco's starting kicker behind a run-heavy, red-zone-efficient offense under Kyle Shanahan.

Missed all three practices last week (Wed-Fri, 9/16-18) sick, drawing a Questionable tag for Week 2 vs. Miami with the 49ers carrying no other kicker on the roster or practice squad. The 49ers worked out veteran kickers Greg Joseph and Younghoe Koo Saturday (9/19) but signed neither — a strong signal the team expects Pineiro to be active and play Sunday (NBC Sports Bay Area, 9/19-20).

Broke out as the overall WR10 in PPR last year (78/1,006/7); locked in as the Z-receiver in new OC Mike LaFleur's scheme with projected 110-120 targets — camp reports have him looking sharper than Marvin Harrison Jr. so far.
Widely projected as the 2026 fantasy #1 overall pick — back-to-back 1,400+ rush-yard seasons plus 60+ catches gives him a McCaffrey-type dual-threat ceiling.
Was seen in a camp "hold-in" (out of pads/helmet) during a portion of a recent practice, though still engaged in drills — worth monitoring, not currently tagged as an injury.
Clear WR1 with essentially no target competition (~30% target share); should produce top-10 WR numbers, with shaky QB play (Michael Penix Jr.) the main swing factor rather than his role.
Finished 2025 as the No. 2 fantasy TE in PPR; projected top-5 again in 2026 as one of Penix's top two targets alongside London.
Consensus QB2 for 2026, but coming off a down 2025 (16.5 PPG, career-low 349 rush yds) due to hamstring/back injuries — real risk, though his efficiency on throws past the sticks remains elite.
Fractured his left wrist coming down awkwardly after a Lamar Jackson end-zone target during Sunday's win over Indianapolis; finished with 1 catch for 11 yards before exiting in the 2nd quarter.

Surgery on the wrist was performed Wednesday morning (Sept 16) and reported successful; Baltimore officially placed him on injured reserve the same day. The NFL's mandatory 4-game minimum rules him out through Week 5 (Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons), with HC Jesse Minter saying he has "a really good chance of coming back here pretty quick" once eligible — Week 6 vs. Cleveland is the target, not yet guaranteed.
Ravens promoted WR Chris Moore from the practice squad to fill the roster spot. Puts his WR2-behind-Flowers breakout runway on hold for at least a month.
Locked in as the top overall fantasy QB — top-9 in passing yards 5 of the last 6 years, top-7 in passing TDs every year, with real rushing/scramble equity on top.

Historic Week 2 Thursday-night performance in a 41-31 win over Detroit: 317 total yards and 5 total TDs (3 pass, 2 rush), over 40 fantasy points — per ESPN, only the 3rd player in NFL history with 9 total TDs and 0 turnovers through a team's first 2 games (Mahomes 2018, Manning 2013 the others).
Led Buffalo's backfield as expected in the opener vs. Houston: 13 carries for 57 yards and 3 catches for 12 yards, though he didn't find the end zone in a game the Bills controlled on the ground.
Signed a 4-year, $48M extension (up to $30M guaranteed) in August 2025, locking him in through 2029.
Sleeper-caliber TE1 upside (80/1,000/10 pace) after a 7 TD, 14.6 YPC 2025 — durability is the real question, but camp reports have his snap share trending up even with Knox/Hawes healthy.
The breakout thesis showed up in real games: 7 catches on 8 targets for 95 yards and a TD in Thursday night's win over Detroit, his best game of the young season.
2025 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year (70/1,014/7); profiles as a safe WR2 (~WR18-20) capped by Carolina's low-volume passing offense, with Jalen Coker now adding real target competition.
Broke out in Carolina's Week 1 loss to Chicago with 8 catches for 138 yards and 2 TDs on 9 targets as the presumptive WR2 behind McMillan.
The ankle rolled in that same game is resolved — logged a full practice Friday (9/18) and was taken off the injury report, clearing him to play Sunday vs. Atlanta (NBC Sports, SI.com, 9/18).

Named the #1 Week 2 waiver-wire target league-wide after his 8-catch, 138-yard, 2-TD Week 1 breakout — now viewed as a legitimate 1A/1B with Tetairoa McMillan rather than a clear WR2 (NFL.com, SI, ESPN).
Chicago's clear RB1 in Ben Johnson's scheme.

The Sept 3 practice scare was cramping, not a leg injury, and it showed no lingering effect — torched Carolina for 18 carries, 124 yards and 3 TDs (plus a catch) in Sunday's 59-37 win, arguably his best game as a Bear.

The Week 2 knee/ankle concern is resolved — logged a full practice Friday (9/18) and was removed from Chicago's injury report entirely, carrying no designation into Sunday's game at Minnesota (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

MRI on Monday (9/21) confirmed a Grade 1 hamstring strain with no tear — Williams "avoided any major injury," per NFL Media's Tom Pelissero, walking back the possible Grade 2 concern flagged Monday morning.

HC Ben Johnson called the imaging news "somewhat encouraging" and said Williams is "week to week" (Chicago Sun-Times, NFL.com, 9/21); Johnson does not expect him to practice at all this week, and while the official tag is DOUBTFUL rather than a hard rule-out, beat reporters (CBS Sports, NBC Sports Philadelphia) characterize him as trending toward missing Week 3 vs. Philadelphia.
No firm return timeline has been announced beyond "week to week" — Grade 1 strains typically run 1-3 weeks, but the Bears have not confirmed an exact game-count target.

Tyson Bagent is lined up to make his first start since 2023 if Williams sits Week 3, after relieving him with 5-of-9 passing for 54 yards in the Week 2 loss to Minnesota; Colston Loveland projects as a key checkdown target with Bagent under center.
Played through the heel contusion and caught 3 of 6 targets for 59 yards in Sunday's opener — remains a solid WR2 with Ja'Marr Chase drawing extra coverage attention.

Played through the back tightness as expected — active and started Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston (Sun 9/20), going 20/31 for 207 yards and 2 TDs (both to Ja'Marr Chase, from 32 and 18 yards) with no INTs, though he did take 5 sacks.
Confirms the back issue was minor/day-to-day as reported all week — no setback, no in-game re-aggravation reported, and no new limitation entering Week 3 prep.
Elite passing-volume QB1 when right — the profile concern remains price/ADP more than health at this point.
Top-5, arguably top-3 PPR RB potential — posted 7 top-12 weekly finishes even through Burrow's 2025 absence; Samaje Perine remains mild committee/handcuff risk.

Backed up a strong Week 1 with 20 carries for 80 yards plus 3 catches on 5 targets in Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston in Week 2 — 42-of-60 snaps, 36 carries and 11 targets through two games confirms bell-cow usage (Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports).

Rookie 1st-round pick competing with fellow rookie Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy for the top WR job — early camp buzz has him leapfrogging Jeudy, though Cleveland's offense projects as one of the league's weakest.
Franchise-tagged ($27.3M) after a 2025 breakout — 93 rec/1,429 yds/9 TD, top-6 PPR WR despite sharing targets with Lamb.
Coming off a down 2025 (75/1,077/3, worst yardage since his rookie year) but still a Round 2 pick — expected bounce-back with Pickens locked in alongside him.
QB7 in fantasy PPG in 2025 (4,552 yds/30 TD/10 INT); with both Lamb and Pickens back, worth drafting as a true QB1.

Left Denver's Week 2 comeback win over Jacksonville (20-13, Sun 9/20) in the 3rd quarter with a hamstring injury after logging 10 carries for 36 yards; ruled questionable to return and didn't come back.

HC Sean Payton called it "a little hamstring" postgame and didn't offer a hard timeline, but a subsequent report (James Palmer, NFL on Prime) described it as a "slight" issue with optimism Dobbins plays Week 3 vs. the Rams — no MRI results were public as of Monday 9/21.

Tyler Badie took over lead work with Dobbins out and RJ Harvey inactive; still Denver's presumed featured back once fully clear, but touch security is in question for Week 3 pending Monday/Tuesday injury reports.
QB15 range if healthy — Denver added Jaylen Waddle to a receiving corps already featuring Sutton/Franklin/Bryant/Mims/Engram, arguably his best supporting cast yet.
Likely slides to a true WR2 role now that Waddle is in town — real target competition caps his ceiling versus prior seasons.
No lingering back/hamstring issue — exploded for 29 carries, 156 yards and 2 TDs plus 5 catches for 30 yards in Sunday's opener, the clear workhorse with Montgomery gone and Isiah Pacheco on IR.

Ground game was quiet in Thursday night's loss to Buffalo (52 yards on 16 carries), but 6 catches and a receiving TD kept his fantasy floor strong — a reminder his receiving work is what makes him a true 3-down workhorse even on an off day rushing.
Top-5 fantasy WR three years running (WR4 in PPG each of the last 3 seasons) — high floor, high ceiling, first-round caliber.
Answered a quiet first half with 9 catches, 142 yards and 2 TDs in Thursday night's loss to Buffalo — his usual bell-cow target share showing up even in a losing effort.
Coming off a big season but genuinely boom/bust (WR41 pace Weeks 1-10 vs. WR13 pace Weeks 11-18) — more of a WR3 with real week-winning upside than a lineup lock.
Favorite for the outside WR spot opposite Watson after a quiet rookie year, but real skepticism here — didn't produce even when Reed/Watson missed time as a rookie.

Initially feared to be a neck injury on Green Bay's second offensive snap of Week 2 vs. the Jets (4-yard catch, hit by Demario Davis) — carted off on a backboard and held in a New York-area hospital overnight for observation (Packers won in OT).

Diagnosis revised Monday (9/21): ESPN's Adam Schefter reports it's actually a back injury, not a neck injury as first reported — meaningfully better news, since neck injuries carry more risk. Feeling and movement in all extremities remains confirmed.

No official return timetable has been announced as of Tuesday 9/22 — the team is still evaluating his recovery, genuinely pending further evaluation rather than a confirmed short absence (Spectrum News, Yahoo Sports). Drops out of the WR2/slot pecking order discussion behind Christian Watson until cleared.

Became the presumptive Packers RB1 once Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL's Commissioner Exempt List (Aug 30) amid a legal case that bars him from the team — Kaleb Johnson (acquired via trade from Pittsburgh) is the complementary back behind Lloyd.
Mixed Week 1 line in the win at Minnesota: 3 sacks and an interception, but gave up 39 points and 239 yards — the offense (led by Christian Watson's big day) bailed out a leaky defensive performance.

Newly added off waivers; Josh Jacobs' ongoing suspension situation (Commissioner's Exempt List) doesn't directly affect this unit, but worth tracking Green Bay's overall team competitiveness if the offense can't keep bailing out shootout-prone defensive outings.
No PUP/injury drama to open 2026 — signed a 4-year, $110.5M extension in June and entered the season atop Green Bay's WR depth chart, fully healthy.
Delivered as the Packers' clear outside WR1 in the Week 1 win at Minnesota: 6 catches for 147 yards and 2 TDs on 8 targets, well ahead of Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed in target share.
Still a fantasy WR1 (ESPN ranks him WR10) — three straight 1,000-yard seasons, 21 TDs over that stretch.

Ruled OUT for the Week 2 game vs. Cincinnati with a Grade 1 hamstring strain; last week's reporting had him as a real candidate to return for Week 3 vs. the Colts, but that optimism reversed Monday (9/21) — a source now says he's NOT expected to play Week 3, and Houston is expected to use the same WR personnel as Week 2 (Yahoo Sports).

HC DeMeco Ryans said Monday only that the team is "still seeing how he progresses"; the ~2-game absence expectation is described as "fluid" rather than locked in — downgraded from Short-Term back to the standard Injury tier given the reversal.
Ranked QB11 for 2026 — with Etienne now gone to New Orleans, more of the offense funnels through Lawrence's arm and legs; expected to throw 30+ TDs for the first time.

Illness that sent him home from a Sept 2 practice was a non-issue by kickoff — logged a full workload in Jacksonville's Week 1 win over Cleveland with 15 carries for 66 yards plus a catch for 22 yards.

Made his long-awaited return from suspension and offseason knee cleanup in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver, playing through it cleanly — 2 catches for 19 yards and a TD on just 2 targets as the offense eased him back in behind Kenneth Walker III's big rushing day.
Expect the target share to climb in Week 2 now that the season-opener workload management is behind him.
A distant WR2 behind Rice — only a 16.1% target share and WR60 finish in 2025; deep-threat/boom upside but not a reliable weekly starter.
Dislocated his right shoulder and suffered a torn labrum colliding with Travis Kelce in the Week 1 win over Denver, missing most of that game, but avoided season-ending surgery per HC Andy Reid.

Played through the shoulder in Week 2 vs. Indianapolis (9/20): 5 catches on 7 targets for 25 yards in the 33-30 OT win — back on the field as hoped, but modest per-target efficiency (5.0 YPT) so far post-labrum injury; worth tracking snap/route share before trusting a big workload.
Posted 286.8 fantasy points in 2025 (10th among QBs); new OC Mike McDaniel plus a healthy starting O-line raises his ceiling, with real rushing upside on top of his passing floor.
Locked in as a starter opposite Ladd McConkey now that Mike Williams retired; still a boom-or-bust profile in a run-first McDaniel scheme.
Reigning NFL MVP — led the league in passing yards (4,707) and TD passes (46) in 2025; real regression risk since his 2025 leaned on unsustainable red-zone efficiency.
Went 22-of-31 for 327 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants; his 426th career passing touchdown moved him past Philip Rivers into 6th all-time (NFL.com, Yahoo Sports).

Confirmed ruled OUT (officially inactive, upgraded from Doubtful) for Sunday's Week 2 game at the Chargers despite going through pregame stretching/route-running under observation from Raiders staff — Las Vegas won 26-14 without him, with Michael Mayer starting again at TE (3 catches/23 yards on 4 targets).

Recovery from the Sept. 8 meniscus trim continues to trend positively: HC Klint Kubiak said Monday (9/21) Bowers is "close, very close" to returning and "looks great" (via Adam Schefter), with Kubiak adding he was optimistic Bowers could've gone Week 2 but ultimately wasn't ready.

Outlook remains on track for a Week 3 return vs. the Saints pending a full/near-full practice week — this softens the earlier Doubtful/game-time-call framing into a firmer, near-term timeline now that the Week 2 absence is confirmed.
Down year by his own standard in 2025 (WR30 overall) but still finished 6th league-wide in target share (28.5%) — new QB Kyler Murray has a track record of feeding elite WR1s.

Backup QB Carson Wentz started Week 2 (Murray in concussion protocol after a late hit in the Week 1 win over Green Bay) — Jefferson was held to 3 catches on 6 targets for 55 yards in a 9-3, rain-soaked win at Chicago, and was candid afterward about the offense's struggles. HC Kevin O'Connell expects Murray back for Week 3 vs. Tampa Bay, so treat this as a one-week dip tied to weather + a backup QB rather than a lasting concern.
Fully cleared post ACL/MCL recovery — no injury designation heading into Week 2 vs. Chicago.

Delivered in the Week 1 win over Green Bay: 4 catches for 36 yards and a 16-yard TD on 5 targets (~66% offensive snap share), 2nd on the team in targets behind Justin Jefferson — looks entrenched as Minnesota's clear TE1 and red-zone option.
Listed RB1 on New England's first unofficial 2026 depth chart ahead of TreVeyon Henderson — handles early-down/short-yardage work.

Rough Week 1 debut of the new-weapons era: 23/33 for 178 yds, 1 TD, but 3 INTs — all in the 4th quarter, including a game-sealing pick in the end zone — in a 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game loss to Seattle. Added 47 rush yds. Called the turnovers "unacceptable" postgame; also lost top target A.J. Brown to an ankle injury mid-game.
Coming off a QB2-overall 2025 (20.7 PPG); Patriots traded for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs, giving him real weapons — widely projected top-5 fantasy QB before Week 1's opener.

Suffered a left knee injury on New York's very first drive of Monday night's 28-6 loss at the Rams, taking a hit from Josaiah Stewart and Byron Young on a 3rd-down deep-ball attempt; ruled out for the rest of the game, with Jameis Winston finishing at QB1 (CBS Sports, NBC New York, Giants.com).

X-rays at SoFi Stadium came back negative; initial fears pointed toward a possible sprained MCL as the likely outcome, with the worse-case ACL/multi-ligament scenario reportedly avoided per early exams (Yahoo Sports, Heavy.com).

An MRI was scheduled for Tuesday (9/22) once the team returned from the West Coast trip; HC John Harbaugh said postgame "we'll know more tomorrow" — exact diagnosis and return timeline still pending as of this writing (Giants.com, Yahoo Sports).

Was the Giants' firmly entrenched starter and a real breakout candidate before this injury (2,200 pass yds/15 TD, plus 480 rush yds/9 rush TD in his rookie stretch); Winston is the next man up if Dart misses time.
Elite volume floor even coming off a down 2025 — earned a 30%+ target share early last season and has topped 23% every year of his career.
Clear backup, not a starter — Breece Hall re-signed and remains the workhorse; Allen competes with Isaiah Davis for change-of-pace touches.

Played through the hamstring that had kept him out of practice all week and caught 3 of 6 targets for 53 yards in the opener with no re-injury reported — Philly's unquestioned WR1 now that A.J. Brown is in New England.

MRI on Monday (9/21) confirmed a sprained MCL in the knee he injured blocking in the 2nd quarter of Sunday's win at Tennessee; ESPN, the Philadelphia Inquirer, and NBC Sports Philadelphia report he's expected to miss "a few weeks" — no exact game count given, and he has not been placed on IR as of 9/22 (an IR move would mean at least 4 games missed, so that outcome isn't yet confirmed).

Depth behind him is thin: rookie 2nd-rounder Eli Stowers (quad/hamstring) and veteran Grant Calcaterra (back) are both already on IR, leaving blocking-oriented Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins as the only healthy TEs on Philly's 53-man roster (Inquirer, ESPN, NBC Sports Philadelphia, 9/21).

Eagles are re-signing 31-year-old Zach Ertz to the practice squad in response to the injury, with a "good chance" he's elevated in time for the Week 3 Monday-night game at the Bears (9/28), per ESPN/Inquirer/NBC Sports Philadelphia and Yahoo Sports/Bleacher Report.

Had opened the season as Philly's clear TE1 (4/77/2 in the Week 1 win over Washington) before this Week 2 injury; profiles as a game-time-decision-to-out for Week 3 with Ertz (once activated), Mundt, and Jenkins as the next-man-up options.

The $16.75M-guaranteed workhorse role is intact when healthy, but he suffered a stinger to his left arm/shoulder on Philadelphia's very first offensive snap of Sunday's 24-20 win at Tennessee (stuffed for no gain by Jeffery Simmons) and missed the rest of the first half.

Returned for the start of the second half but played sparingly before exiting again in the 4th quarter — finished with just 4 carries for 9 yards and 1 catch for 11 yards; postgame he said only "I'm all right, we'll know more later in the week" and was set for an MRI.

As of Monday 9/21, MRI results/official diagnosis had not yet been reported publicly — genuinely uncertain/pending imaging, consistent with a Questionable-caliber stinger rather than a confirmed structural injury.

Handled the clear early-down workload before exiting: 13 carries for 52 yards plus a catch for 8 yards in Sunday's 31-7 win at Arizona (Drew Lock starting for the injured Sam Darnold), before leaving in the second half — officially Questionable to return, then held out.

HC Mike Macdonald clarified Monday (9/21) the injury is actually near the shoulder, not the chest as first reported, calling it shoulder "intact" and "nothing serious"; X-rays remain negative and Week 3 practice participation will determine his availability (SI).
While Zach Charbonnet opens the season on PUP (ACL recovery), Seattle is running a real 3-way rotation with George Holani and Emanuel Wilson rather than handing Price a clean bell-cow role.
Signed a massive 5-yr/$265M extension; finished as a QB1-range fantasy scorer in every full season as a starter, behind a receiving corps upgraded with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk.

The ankle rehab and conflicting reports resolved in his favor for Week 1 — played and produced in Tampa Bay's opener vs. Dallas, catching 4 targets for 40 yards plus a 3-yard carry, confirming the WR2/target-lead role behind Emeka Egbuka now that Mike Evans is gone.

But he left that game with a hamstring injury, missed practice all week (Sept 16-17), and has been confirmed ruled OUT for Week 2 vs. Cleveland (correcting the opponent — not New Orleans). Reporting indicates the strain isn't believed to be severe, but no return timeline beyond Week 2 has been confirmed yet.
Entrenched starter chasing a 5th straight 1,000-yard season — hit 1,000 rushing yards in each of the past 4 years.
Returned to practice Wednesday after minor foot soreness — no real Week 1 concern, still ahead of Tyjae Spears on the depth chart.

Dislocated his left elbow late in the first half of Washington's Week 2 loss to Dallas (Sun 9/20) — his second dislocation of the same elbow in under a year (first was Nov. 2, 2025 vs. Seattle, which cost him 3 weeks before a Week-14 reinjury ended his 2025 season).

X-rays showed no fracture, but Daniels underwent further imaging Monday (9/21) and Washington has NOT yet announced an official diagnosis or return timetable; HC Dan Quinn said only that he "anticipates" Daniels returning this season. One outside sports-medicine estimate pegged a simple dislocation at ~3-6 weeks vs. 6-10+ weeks if there's ligament damage — genuinely pending imaging results, not team-confirmed.
Elite, high-ceiling QB1 talent when healthy (top-5 fantasy QB in 2024) — but recurrence of the same elbow injury adds real season-long variance until Washington clarifies severity.
Washington enters 2026 near the top of the league in vacated targets/air yards; his rough 2025 (38/582/3 in 10 games) looks like an outlier tied to a holdout and injuries rather than decline.
Reigning Super Bowl champs and the #1-ranked defense in 2026 projections — led the NFL in scoring defense and led the league with 7 defensive/ST TDs in 2025. Elite, high-floor DST1.

Worth monitoring: starting QB Sam Darnold left the Sept 9 opener with a hip injury; a Sept 10 MRI ruled out major structural damage but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona — a Drew Lock-led offense for that game could mean tougher field position/offensive support for the defense.

Back-to-back DST7 finishes with Vic Fangio adding Jonathan Greenard and Riq Woolen to an already deep room. Opens vs. WSH and TEN (favorable), but carries the toughest full-season DST schedule of any team in 2026.
2nd-best fantasy DST in 2025, then added Myles Garrett and revamped the secondary this offseason — projected top-3 unit for 2026 with a strong offense limiting bad field position.
Top-10 in sacks and takeaways in 2025; opens 2026 vs. Arizona and Las Vegas, called the best 2-game starting schedule of any DST — legitimate top-10 season-long upside.

Top-10 fantasy finish in 2025, but that leaned on a soft schedule; added Dre'Mont Jones, Kevin Byard, and a 2nd-round pick. Real talent additions, but a much tougher 2026 slate makes them a regression candidate off last year's ranking.

Top-5 fantasy unit two years running under HC DeMeco Ryans, ranked 2nd for 2026 behind only Seattle — led the NFL in fantasy points per game (56.4) last season. Opens with tougher matchups (BUF, then CIN).

DST5 in points per game in 2025 (7.8 PPG) even with T.J. Watt missing three games, powered by 27 forced turnovers and 48 sacks. Secondary got shredded at times — free agents Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker were brought in to fix that, but this remains one of the league's oldest defensive units.

Played through the high-ankle sprain that had him Questionable and delivered his first extended workload: 11 carries for 41 yards and a TD plus 2 catches for 9 yards in Sunday's game vs. the Chargers.
No setback reported after the game — the ankle no longer looks like a Week 2 concern with a full game under his belt.
New OC Mike LaFleur is moving him around the formation more; averaged 12.8 PPG over his last 5 healthy 2025 games (low-end WR1 pace).
No current 2026 injury or concussion concern found — fully past the foot/heel issues that limited him late last season.

Exploded for 5 catches, 150 yards and a 54-yard TD in the first half of Baltimore's Week 1 win over Indianapolis before a recurring hamstring injury (first tweaked in joint practices with the Vikings, then re-aggravated in that Week 1 game) forced him out for the second half.
Officially ruled OUT for Sunday vs. New Orleans — the Ravens announced the decision Saturday (9/19), upgraded from Friday's Doubtful tag to a confirmed absence.

Firmed up Monday (9/21): HC Jesse Minter said Flowers has a "good shot" to play Week 3 vs. Dallas — an upgrade from the prior generic "hope remains" framing (Newsweek). Rashod Bateman steps up as Baltimore's top receiver and Mark Andrews' target share rises with Flowers out in the meantime.
Turns 32; 2025 was still elite (1,595 yds / 16 TD) with no decline signs yet, but a new play-caller and remade O-line add real variance this year.

Showed zero decline signs in the Week 1 opener vs. Indianapolis: 24 carries for 144 yards and 3 rushing TDs (35.3 fantasy pts) as Baltimore's clear lead back, with only Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali behind him on the depth chart.

Week 2 usage raised a flag: 16 carries for 68 yards and a TD plus 3 catches for 19 yards in the loss to New Orleans, but no explosive runs (long of 8 yards) and he was "puzzlingly" limited to just 5 carries in the second half even while Baltimore led — worth monitoring, not yet a confirmed workload cut (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Baltimore Beatdown).

The camp ankle sprain was a non-issue — played through it in Week 1 vs. Baltimore (7 catches, 88 yards on 12 targets) and again in Buffalo's Week 2 Thursday-night win at Detroit (6.8 fantasy pts), with no re-aggravation reported either week.

Confirmed trade (official March 11, 2026, roster move finalized Aug 17): Bears sent Moore plus a 2026 5th-round pick to Buffalo for a 2026 2nd-round pick. Bills guaranteed $15.5M of his 2028 salary, and the trade also guaranteed his 2027 salary — reshapes the WR room alongside Shakir.

Followed a strong Week 1 (21.0 fantasy pts) with a scary exit from Thursday night's Week 2 win over Detroit: dropped a would-be TD, then landed hard on his left shoulder late in the 2nd quarter and was ruled out at halftime. Diagnosis is in as of Friday (9/19) — an AC joint sprain, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport — and ESPN's Adam Schefter reports doctors "do not consider it serious"; he's day-to-day, though "not a lock" for Week 3 vs. the Chargers. Revised from Thursday's unconfirmed-severity language now that the imaging/diagnosis is back.

The camp hamstring issue was fully behind him for the opener — played through it and led Carolina's backfield in the Week 1 loss to Chicago: 10 carries for 49 yards and a rush TD plus 3 catches for 38 yards and a receiving TD (23.7 fantasy pts).
Listed RB1 over Jonathon Brooks, but Carolina is running a real 1A/1B committee to open the year.

Re-aggravated the groin injury that sidelined him late in camp during Carolina's Week 2 win over Atlanta (34-3, Sun 9/20) — exited in the 4th quarter after just 5 carries and 1 catch and did not return.

Tom Pelissero (NFL Network) reported Monday (9/21) that Brooks is "week-to-week" and is seeking additional medical opinions — no firm return date attached, which is why his tag moved from Questionable to Doubtful ahead of Week 3 (9/27 at Cleveland) (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT).
Still described as not a long-term/season-ending issue and no IR move has been reported as of Tuesday 9/22, but the Panthers haven't given a formal practice-status update yet this week.
Chuba Hubbard (22 carries, 102 yards, 1 TD through two games) is "due for a larger workload" Week 3 if Brooks sits, with AJ Dillon next in line for the RB2 role (CBS Sports/SI Onsi, Heavy.com).
The groin injury was fully resolved for Week 1 — played through it with no setback, catching all 5 targets for 63 yards vs. Carolina.

The mid-August hyperextended knee that had him week-to-week was a non-issue by Week 1 — carried 10 times for 100 yards and a TD behind Swift in the win over Carolina, clear RB2 on Chicago's depth chart.

The hamstring injury is resolved — returned to a full practice Friday (9/18) and was removed from the injury report, carrying no designation into Sunday's game vs. Minnesota (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/18).

Played through the calf injury that had him Questionable into the weekend and finished with 2 catches for 52 yards on 3 targets as Chicago routed Carolina 59-37 — light volume, but more a function of the blowout game script than the calf, which held up with no setback reported.
Remains Caleb Williams' clear WR1 with DJ Moore traded away; expect target share to normalize now that the calf is no longer a question.
Moore's departure opens a big target vacuum; Bears leaning into more 13-personnel — projected ~78 rec/918 yds/7 TD after closing his rookie year red-hot.
2025 1st-round pick (10th overall, Michigan).

Played through the knee hyperextension with no setback, though production was quiet in the opener — 2 catches for 12 yards on 4 targets vs. Tampa Bay. Role and target volume are unchanged; treat it as a one-game blip rather than a trend.
Moved to the unambiguous RB1 spot on Cleveland's depth chart, ahead of Sampson and Sanders.
Battling a minor "nagging" injury that cost him two camp practices, but coaches aren't concerned — remains Cleveland's clear lead back over Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, and Ahmani Marshall.
2025 2nd-round pick (36th overall, Ohio State), acquired via a Day 1 trade with Jacksonville.

Handled 12 of Cleveland's 15 RB carries plus 5 catches (17 touches, 48 total yards) in the Week 2 win over Tampa Bay, confirming him as the clear #1 back even in a tough matchup (CBS Sports, RotoWire).
Led the Browns in receiving as a rookie (72/731/6); with Njoku gone he's the unquestioned TE1 under new OC Todd Monken, who developed Andrews and Likely.

The hip flare-up was a non-issue once games started — produced in both Week 1 (9.8 fantasy pts, opener vs. New Orleans) and Week 2 (17.2 fantasy pts in Thursday night's win over Buffalo), with no re-aggravation reported.
Confirmed "full-go" for Week 1 vs. Minnesota after full-contact clearance and full participation in a joint practice vs. Arizona — a clean upgrade off the torn ACL, though still his first year back.

Pleaded no contest Sept 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal-damage charges from the May incident — fined $1,000 plus costs, with the damage charge to be dismissed after a 12-month deferred agreement.

The legal resolution does NOT end his NFL absence: he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (can't practice, play, or be on the 53-man roster, though he's paid and can attend meetings/individual workouts) while a separate personal-conduct-policy review continues. Sources still peg the likely suspension range at 4-6 games once announced, with games missed on the exempt list expected to count toward it.

New as of 9/22: the accuser's attorneys filed a motion to permanently seal case evidence, and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the NFL's investigation is ongoing with a suspension announcement possibly coming "sooner rather than later" — length still not officially set (Pro Football Rumors, Yahoo Sports).

Green Bay has already hedged, trading a 2028 6th-round pick to Pittsburgh for RB Kaleb Johnson as depth-chart insurance — a real sign the team isn't banking on a quick Jacobs return. Treat him as unplayable/bench for now.
The minor calf injury was a non-issue — played through it with no setback in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore, catching 2 of 4 targets for 37 yards.

Re-injured the same left heel that had March surgery late in the 1st quarter of Sunday night's loss at Kansas City — couldn't put weight on it, was carted to the locker room, and left the stadium on crutches in a walking boot; X-rays came back negative that night.

Ian Rapoport (NFL Network) reported Pierce will attempt to rehab rather than have immediate surgery, and is expected to miss "several weeks," with a best-case return "midseason" — revised from Monday's no-timeline-yet uncertainty to a real multi-week-plus absence (ESPN, NFL.com).

Colts HC Shane Steichen said Tuesday (9/22) he "didn't know" if Pierce could play Week 3 vs. Houston, with further testing still pending; multiple outlets (WANE-TV, Stampede Blue) report Pierce is expected to land on IR, which would lock him out a minimum of 4 games, though it's not yet officially transacted.

Colts signed veteran WR Darius Slayton as a direct injury replacement; expect targets to spread toward Josh Downs (top beneficiary), Keenan Allen, Slayton, and TE Tyler Warren (NBC Sports/PFT, DraftSharks).
The groin injury fully resolved — played through the Week 1 loss to Baltimore with no setback, catching 3 of 5 targets for 13 yards and a receiving TD.
Traded from LV to Jacksonville to bolster a banged-up WR room.

The thumb injury from an August joint practice vs. Carolina remains a lingering, week-to-week nuisance — limited again in Friday's (9/18) practice — but carries no Week 2 designation; RotoWire/CBS Sports/NBC Sports (9/18) confirm he's ready to play Sunday at Denver after catching both his targets for 40 yards and a TD in Week 1.
Jacksonville's clear WR1 — left the Week 1 win over Cleveland in the 2nd quarter with a shoulder injury but returned before halftime and finished with 3 catches for 40 yards.
The shoulder issue is resolved — practiced fully Friday (9/18) and was removed from Jacksonville's injury report entirely, with no designation for Sunday's game at Denver (NBC Sports, 9/18).
Stepped up in practice reps amid Thomas/Meyers injuries in one of the league's deepest WR rooms, alongside Travis Hunter.

The preseason ankle swelling (per HC Andy Reid, caused by his shoe) was a non-issue — exploded in his Chiefs debut on Monday Night Football vs. Denver with 23 carries for 173 yards and a rushing TD, plus 3 catches for 18 yards and a receiving TD (2 total TDs).
Immediately looks like the clear lead back in Kansas City's backfield after the free-agent signing (3yr/$43.05M).

Backed up the Week 1 explosion with another workhorse Week 2 outing: 24 carries for 117 yards plus 6 catches for 61 yards (178 total) in KC's 33-30 OT win over Indianapolis (9/20) — no TD after being stuffed on 3 straight plays from the 1-yard line. Two games in, he's playing every-down back.

The lingering "knee" injury-report notation from his offseason ACL/LCL recovery was a non-factor in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver — went 15/27 for 184 yards and 2 passing TDs (1 INT) and added 7 carries for 23 yards and a rushing TD.
Now 37, the oldest TE in the league; production down two straight years (11.4 PPG in 2025, worst since 2015) — projected for a further step down (74/770/4).

New hamstring injury (first surfaced after Denver's Week 1 loss at Kansas City) worsened rather than resolved — after DNP Wednesday and limited practices Thursday/Friday, Harvey was ultimately downgraded and ruled INACTIVE for Week 2 vs. Jacksonville, contradicting the earlier "trending toward Questionable, real chance to play" reporting.

No MRI results or firm return timeline have been reported publicly as of Monday 9/21 — outlets note severity/duration remains unconfirmed, so treat as a genuine week-to-week situation rather than a known short absence.
With Harvey out, J.K. Dobbins led Denver's Week 2 backfield work (until his own hamstring exit) and rookie Jonah Coleman saw increased snaps — Harvey's touches evaporate whenever he's out.

The camp hamstring strain was fully resolved for Week 1 with Denver, but the passing-game role was thin in his Broncos debut — just 1 catch for 2 yards on 3 targets as Courtland Sutton and the run game dominated the offense.
Worth monitoring whether target share improves in Week 2 now that he's fully healthy, or whether Denver's offense simply doesn't feed him volume.
Real committee with David Montgomery — locked into 3rd-down/receiving work and kick returns rather than a clean backup role.

Trade acquisition from DET leads the Houston backfield, and Joe Mixon's release clears out the only other real competition — but Woody Marks still holds real passing-down/receiving touches, so it remains a genuine committee, not a clear lead back.
Carries no injury designation heading into Week 1 vs. Arizona — the ambiguity from his Aug 27 preseason-finale kickoff hit has cleared, and he's back handling the full kicking/kickoff workload.

Played through the Week 1 rib injury (suffered on a hit from Mack Wilson vs. Arizona) in Sunday's Week 2 win over the Raiders, wearing a flak jacket for protection — caught 4 of 6 targets for 39 yards and a TD in the 31-14 win.
No setback or re-aggravation reported; the rib did not limit his workload and he remains the Chargers' clear top target earner.
Rookie hype exceeds his current role — projected ~250 att/1,125 yds, but likely won't clear 70% snap share with Mitchell handling passing downs. High-variance breakout, not a lock.

Hip injury (HC Sean McVay says distinct from the earlier groin/psoas soreness) cost him back-to-back DNPs — Friday (9/18) and Saturday (9/19) — and the Rams ultimately ruled him OUT/inactive for Monday Night Football vs. the Giants (9/21); he did not play, and his season stat line remains frozen at 5 catches/74 yards from Week 1 (NFL.com, ESPN).

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported pregame Monday that Nacua was "trending towards not playing," though the Rams held out hope he'd test it in warmups; no confirmed diagnosis or return timeline (and no IR move) has been reported as of Tuesday 9/22 — genuinely uncertain week-to-week status heading into Week 3.

Separately, the civil lawsuit over the alleged biting incident/antisemitic remark now has a set trial date of March 27, 2028; Nacua has not been criminally charged and was not placed on the NFL's commissioner exempt list, with Schefter noting "a real possibility" he avoids any in-season discipline (Yahoo Sports/Deseret News).
Turns 33; 2025 TD rate was unsustainable (49% of his fantasy points came via red-zone scores vs. a 14.5% NFL average) and his catch rate hit a career-low 53%.
No longer the clear #1 target with Nacua sharing the offense — real regression risk.

Answered the regression question emphatically in Monday night's 28-6 rout of the Giants: 8 catches for 195 yards and 2 TDs, Stafford's clear top target with Nacua (hip) inactive (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports).
Remains the lead back in a McVay-preferred ~65:35 split with Blake Corum — not under real threat, but not a bell-cow either.

Split carries close to even with Blake Corum in Monday night's win over the Giants (12-85-0 rush plus a receiving TD for Williams), and lost a fumble at his own 11 late in the first half — worth tracking whether the committee trends more even going forward (CBS Sports/RotoWire).
RB2 behind Kyren Williams in a ~65:35 split that has been fluid through camp.

Carried a near-even Monday-night workload alongside Kyren Williams (combined 164 rush yards) in the win over the Giants — the split continues to run closer to 50/50 than a clean Williams-lead role (CBS Sports/RotoWire).
Elevated to Rams' primary kicker after a strong rookie year: 18/19 FG, 48/48 PAT.
Joshua Karty demoted to backup (not cut) — Mevis holds the job outright for now.

The Aug 23 ankle sprain was a non-issue for the Sept 13 opener — Jeanty was off the injury report entirely and delivered a workhorse Week 1 in Las Vegas' game vs. Miami: 23 carries for 102 yards plus 6 catches for 45 yards and 2 receiving TDs (27 touches, 2 total TDs).
Confirmed as the clear lead back over rookie Mike Washington Jr., who saw no meaningful role in Week 1.

Reaffirmed the workhorse role with 25 total touches (21 carries/48 yards, 4-of-7 targets/15 yards) in the Raiders' 26-14 upset of the Chargers in Week 2, but had a late-game injury scare (returned to finish the game) and dropped 3 passes — worth a brief watch, not yet a designation change (CBS Sports, NBC Sports).
No current injury flag, but missed time each of the last two seasons plus offseason shoulder surgery.
New OC Jeff Hafley is planning a massive workload (40-touch game talk) — huge weekly ceiling, real durability risk.

Placed on injured reserve Sept 16 after further evaluation of the sore thumb from Minnesota's Week 1 win over Green Bay revealed a fracture requiring surgery — HC Kevin O'Connell said the exact moment of the break is unclear, but it escalated from what first looked like a bruise.

IR's mandatory 4-game minimum rules him out through Week 5 (vs. Bears, at Bucs, vs. Dolphins, at Saints); O'Connell called the recovery "not expected to be long-term" beyond that window, putting a realistic return at Week 6 or later with no hard date confirmed.
Minnesota promoted RB DeeJay Dallas from the practice squad and signed Jerome Ford to the practice squad as depth behind Aaron Jones.

Was co-starter on paper with Jordan Mason, who had outproduced him in camp and Week 1 — but Mason's Sept 16 thumb-fracture surgery and IR placement (out a mandatory 4 games minimum, through at least Week 5) hands Jones the clear lead-back role in Minnesota for at least a month.
Depth behind him is thin (DeeJay Dallas up from the practice squad), so expect a season-high workload the next several weeks — flagged by multiple outlets as a real workload winner.
Rough 2025: a 3-game suspension to start the year, only 17.4% target share (Jefferson had 28.2%), finished WR43.
QB upgrade to Kyler Murray helps, but MIN also signed WR Jauan Jennings — adds competition rather than clearing it. Profiles more WR3/bench right now.
Missed the Week 1 loss to Seattle (ruled out Sept 8) after not practicing all week with an ankle injury; Rhamondre Stevenson started in his place.

Returned to practice Sept 14 and was a full participant in Wednesday's (Sept 16) practice, an upgrade that has him tracking to play Sunday's Week 2 home opener vs. Pittsburgh — officially cleared to Active.
Expect a real but complementary role behind Stevenson (who keeps the early-down/pass-pro work) — figure roughly 10-12 touches in a space/change-of-pace role rather than a even split.

Left his Patriots debut early in the 3rd quarter of the Sept 9 NFL Kickoff Game (a 13-10 loss to Seattle) with a right ankle injury after Seahawks CB Nehemiah Pritchett's knee landed on his ankle; had 3 catches for 26 yds on 4 targets before exiting.

Thursday's (Sept 10) MRI confirmed a high-ankle sprain (Tuesday-night X-rays had been negative). Confirmed Sept 11 (AP): Patriots are placing him on injured reserve, officially ruling him out a minimum of four games under IR roster rules — New England is also signing DT DaQuan Jones as a separate roster move. Treat him as unplayable through at least Week 4.

Arrived via trade from PHI (Patriots sent Philadelphia a 2028 1st-round pick and a 2027 5th-round pick); signed for up to $112.75M with $32.75M guaranteed. Was stepping into a wide-open target share atop New England's WR room before the injury.
Signed in free agency; profiles as a high-volume slot piece similar to Diggs' old role now that Diggs is gone.
Hamstring injury in an August joint practice vs JAX; placed on IR with a return designation — out at least the first 4 games.

Played through the minor hamstring issue with no setback — caught 8 of 10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-17 win over Baltimore, giving him an 18-268-1 line on 23 targets through two games as the Saints' clear top downfield target.

Torched Detroit for 10/182 in the Week 1 opener; the Thursday-emergent hamstring tag never became a real threat — Adam Schefter and Saints beat reporters expected him to play all week, and that's exactly what happened.
Signed a 4-yr/$52M deal with hometown New Orleans as a free agent and is listed as the starter.
Alvin Kamara remains on the roster (health TBD) alongside Kendre Miller — real early-season committee risk.

Left Monday night's loss at the Rams late in the 1st quarter with a right shoulder injury on a contested 50/50 ball vs. CB Trent McDuffie, officially tagged questionable to return, but came back in the 2nd quarter and played the rest of the game (NY Giants team X/Ian Rapoport, Yahoo Sports).
Said postgame his shoulder "popped out" but described it as "OK"; X-rays were planned once the team got back to New Jersey, with no fracture or tear reported as of 9/22 (Yahoo Sports, Heavy.com).

Finished with just 1 catch for 1 yard in the loss, down from his Week 1 SNF opener (6 catches/9 targets/69 yards) — workload was capped further by Jaxson Dart's first-drive exit and Jameis Winston playing most of the game.

No new reports of a setback to the surgically repaired knee from last season's ACL/meniscus tear; continued recovery/workload buildup remains the longer-term watch item alongside this new shoulder scare.

Fully cleared from last year's gruesome rookie ankle injury (dislocation + open fracture) and confirmed as the Giants' Week 1 starting RB over Tyrone Tracy Jr., hosting Dallas on Sunday Night Football.

Held to just 12 carries for 36 yards, 4 catches for 19 yards, and a lost fumble in Monday night's 28-6 loss at the Rams — the whole Giants game plan was wrecked after QB Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury on the first series (182 total team yards); treat the poor box score as game-script-driven, not a role change (RotoWire, CBS Sports).
Signed for 3yr/$40M+, now the clear TE1 ahead of Theo Johnson, reunited with HC John Harbaugh — real path to a top-10 fantasy TE role after sharing looks with Mark Andrews in Baltimore.
Groin was a non-issue — ran for 102 yards and a TD on 22 carries plus 2 catches for 16 yards in Sunday's opener vs. Tennessee, his best workload in well over a year.
20th overall pick, stepping into the WR2 role behind DeVonta Smith with A.J. Brown gone.
Hamstring strain in camp plus Philly's low-volume passing scheme caps his rookie-year ceiling — realistic WR4 as a rookie.
His camp hamstring strain is also trending back toward full practice participation as of Sept 3.

Trade finalized March 9, 2026: Colts sent him plus a 2026 7th-round pick to Pittsburgh for a 2026 6th-round pick — as part of the trade-and-sign, the Steelers also signed him to a new 3-year, $59M contract.
Downgraded to OUT for Week 2 at New England with a foot injury, ruled out Saturday (9/19) after missing practice Thursday and Friday — reversing Friday's earlier removal from the injury report.

HC Mike Tomlin/staff (via Mike McCarthy, offensive coordinator, Tue 9/22) put Pittman in Wednesday's evaluation group and said there's no clear feel yet on Week 3 availability — still genuinely uncertain, no timeline set (SI). DK Metcalf remains the clear #1 in his absence, with Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard in line for more snaps.

Played through the previously undisclosed issue with no setback and led Pittsburgh's offense with 10 targets, turning them into 4 catches for 40 yards in the opener vs. Atlanta — the target volume was there even if the per-catch efficiency wasn't.
Traded from Seattle to Pittsburgh in 2025 (Steelers sent a 2nd- and 7th-rounder, got back a 6th) and signed a 5-year, $150M extension there.

Suffered a toe injury on a pass-blocking/fumble-recovery rep in the 2nd quarter of Sunday's loss to New England, was carted to the locker room, returned for a few series coming out of halftime, then appeared to re-aggravate it and was ruled out for good; finished with 9 total touches for 44 yards.
No MRI results or return timeline had been reported as of Monday (9/21); HC Mike McCarthy had no postgame update on severity — worth confirming before Week 3.
With Dowdle sidelined, Travis Homer picked up early-down work behind Jaylen Warren, adding more uncertainty to an already crowded Pittsburgh backfield committee.

Confirmed as Pittsburgh's Week 1 RB1 on the team's own depth chart over Rico Dowdle, and it held up in the box score — out-touched Dowdle 15-10 (10 carries/46 yards plus 5 catches/27 yards) in the Week 1 win, the more involved back in both the run and pass game.
Signed a 2-year extension through 2027 (~$17.5M total, $12M guaranteed) in September 2025.

Opened 2026 with 8 catches for 122 yds and the game-winning 45-yard TD (41 YAC) on 4th-and-1 in the 4th quarter of Seattle's 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game win over New England — early sign the regression fears may be overblown.

Backup QB Drew Lock (18/22, 187 yds) finished that game after starter Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive; Darnold's Thursday (Sept 10) MRI showed no major structural damage ("dodged a bullet," per the team), but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona with Lock confirmed as the Week 2 starter — worth tracking since it affects who's throwing Smith-Njigba the ball.
Led all NFL WRs with 1,793 yds/10 TD in 2025 and won Offensive Player of the Year; now the highest-paid WR in history (4yr/$168.6M).
Top-5 overall fantasy asset — the question is regression off a historic year, not upside.
Full workhorse usage in the opener with no ill effects from the calf scare: 10 carries for 68 yards plus 5 catches for 20 yards in the win over the Rams.
Held out of the end zone, but the touch volume is exactly what you want to see after last year's injury history.

HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed this week the Week 1 split with rookie Kaelon Black (who out-carried him 14-10, 44% of snaps) was a deliberate plan to lighten McCaffrey's load: "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more... love taking some off Christian." Total touches were even (15-15), but expect Black to keep chipping into the carry share.

Left San Francisco's Week 2 blowout win over Miami (49ers up 35-6) early in the 4th quarter with a hip injury, after wincing following a 27-yard catch-and-run in the 3rd quarter that set up a Christian McCaffrey TD; finished 3-for-3 on targets for 54 yards before exiting.

HC Kyle Shanahan said postgame the injury is not believed to be serious and that Evans would have stayed in the game had it been closer — reads as blowout-game caution more than a real injury concern.

Monday (9/21) update: Shanahan said the hip "will have to be managed this week" and Evans will likely miss some practice time, but gave no indication Evans is expected to miss Week 3 vs. Arizona (NBC Sports). Turns 33 in August — an aging watch item independent of this injury.
Played in the opener as expected off Achilles recovery, but usage was light (2 catches, 12 yards on 5 targets, 46.2% of snaps) — matches Shanahan's stated plan to manage his snap count.

The Achilles maintenance plan wrapped up clean — upgraded to a full practice Friday (9/18) and removed from the injury report entirely, with no designation for Sunday vs. Miami; Wed/Thu limited reps were confirmed as planned workload management, not a new setback (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

Diagnosed with a deltoid ligament sprain in his left ankle (not an Achilles issue — HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed the Achilles is intact) after leaving the Sept 10 opener vs. the Rams early without a target.

Underwent ankle surgery Wednesday (Sept 16) after the injury proved worse than initially believed, and was officially placed on injured reserve — revised from the earlier ~1-month outlook to a firmer ~10-week absence per Shanahan's post-surgery update.
Drop-and-stash-if-needed territory in shallow leagues for the next couple of months. Still a real deep-league breakout stash for whenever SF's WR room opens back up.
Two straight down seasons (sub-12 PPG each) with the worst YPRR marks of his career and a shrinking red-zone role.
Back in SF on a 1-year “reunion” deal — real chance 2026 is his last fantasy-relevant year.
The camp toe sprain didn't cost him any time — played through it in the Week 1 opener vs. Cincinnati, catching 5 of 6 targets for 63 yards.
Locked in as Tampa Bay's WR1 with Mike Evans gone to SF.

Lost the early-season timeshare battle in practice — actual Week 1-2 usage has run heavily toward Irving (just 23 snaps/2 carries in Week 2 vs. Cleveland), not the 50/50 split the depth chart listing implied. A passing-down role is the main remaining value.
Left Pittsburgh (where he was the 2025 Team MVP) and signed a 2-year, $14M free-agent deal with Tampa Bay in March 2026.

Correction on the committee framing — Week 2 usage was lopsided in his favor: 51 snaps to Gainwell's 23, 19 touches to 5 (17 carries/89 yards, 4 catches/1 yard) in the 23-19 loss to Cleveland (9/20), after a similarly Irving-favored Week 1. Looks like the clear lead back, not a 50/50 split despite the depth chart listing.
No lingering concussion concern — caught 5 of 6 targets for 38 yards in Sunday's opener vs. the Jets, a solid underneath role in Tennessee's offense.
Took a hard hit in Monday practice and missed Wednesday's session with dizziness/stiffness — evaluated but not diagnosed with a concussion, has since returned to practice with no Week 1 concern.
Rookie WR with rising fantasy stock as the direct beneficiary any time Wan'Dale Robinson is banged up.
2026 1st-round pick (No. 4 overall, Ohio State) — Tennessee's top rookie weapon for Cam Ward alongside slot man Wan'Dale Robinson.

Wasn't the clear lead back in Week 2 — White out-snapped him 36-23 in the Dallas loss (9/20) as the Commanders leaned on White's receiving in a trailing game script. Treat this as a genuine 2-man committee rather than a locked-in CM1 role, even after his confirmed Week 1 lead-back role vs. Philadelphia.

Bounced back with the clearer role in Week 2 vs. Dallas (37-20 loss, 9/20): out-snapped Croskey-Merritt 36-23, leaned on heavily as a receiver in catch-up mode — 7 carries/43 yards + 6 catches/40 yards (83 total). A real 2-man committee, and he may now have the passing-down edge.
Signed a one-year, $2M free-agent deal with Washington after his rookie contract with Tampa Bay expired — reunites him with Arizona State teammate Jayden Daniels.
Turns 33 in November, but 2025 metrics (9.9 YPT, top-7 YPRR) show no real decline — his route-running game tends to age gracefully.
Signed 1yr/$12M as Washington's presumed WR2 behind Terry McLaurin, throwing to Jayden Daniels.
Led the NFL with 323 carries in 2025 — 1,585 yds, 18 rush TD, RB1 overall.
New contract extension cements him as the Colts' offensive centerpiece; staff may trim touches slightly to manage wear, but role security is elite.
New extension (announced Aug 6, 2026): 2 years, $44M ($39M guaranteed, up to $47M) — the 2nd-highest-paid RB in the NFL by AAV.
2025: 126 rec/1,239 yds/11 TD, led all TEs in target share (25.4%).

New Cardinals staff invested heavily in the run game (drafted RB Jeremiyah Love 3rd overall, signed Tyler Allgeier) — his 683-route workload likely won't repeat. Still a top-2 TE, just not a top-15-overall ceiling.
New 3-yr/$24M deal after a career year: 252 att, 1,201 yds, 11 TD.
Backups Davis, Blue, and Mafah are unproven; Dallas' history of a 2-RB rotation still leaves him high touch security.
No 2026 camp or preseason injury reports; practiced fully through August, including joint sessions vs NE.
Standard top-5 fantasy QB profile — the rushing floor keeps him there even on off passing days.
2025 was a down year (28th pressure rate, 31st sack rate) after a top-12 2024.
Added DC Anthony Weaver plus EDGE Trey Hendrickson and DL Calais Campbell up front. Soft early slate (IND, NO, DAL, TEN, ATL, CLE) — good streaming value.

Locked in as the Raiders' starting TE while Brock Bowers recovers from a Sept 8 meniscus trim — the timeline has since been walked back from "a game or two" toward a more realistic Week 3 return, extending Mayer's runway as a real streaming/flex option beyond just Week 1.

In the NFL's concussion protocol after a first-quarter hit in the Week 1 win over Green Bay; HC Kevin O'Connell said Sept 15 Murray "came in feeling pretty good today" but the team is taking his return "a day at a time."

Was a limited practice participant Wednesday and Thursday while working through the protocol — O'Connell said he'd cleared 3 of 5 protocol phases as of Thursday and needs to reach full clearance (Phase 5) by Friday to have a chance to play. Not yet confirmed cleared; Carson Wentz (who threw for 133 yds/3 TD in relief in Week 1) is the likely starter at Chicago (Sept 20) if Murray isn't cleared in time.

Locked in as Cincinnati's starting kicker after a standout training camp and preseason — didn't miss a kick in camp, including a 65-yard practice bomb, and drilled a 58-yard field goal in preseason play.
Steady weekly floor as the No. 1 leg on a high-scoring Bengals offense; added off waivers to fill the roster's kicker spot.

Cleared the Thursday-emergent groin injury with no issue — played all of Sunday's 35-13 blowout win over Miami, logging 16 of San Francisco's 45 snaps (down from Week 1's 43.8% share), a clear step back toward a standard backup role.

Finished with 7 carries for 25 yards (no catches, no targets) vs. McCaffrey's 10 carries and 2 TDs — after out-carrying CMC 14-10 in the Week 1 opener, the workload swung decisively back to McCaffrey once SF built a big lead. Treat Black as a real CMC handcuff, not a standalone weekly play, for now.

Third-round rookie (No. 75 overall) who opened as Miami's Week 1 starter (50/55 snaps) and led the Dolphins in receiving with 5/94 on 7 targets — through two weeks has carved out real snaps in a crowded receiver room.

Left Miami's Week 2 loss to the 49ers (35-13) with a right ankle injury with 7:50 left in the 4th quarter after catching 2 of 3 targets for 19 yards; walked off under his own power but was seen leaving the locker room in a walking boot.

HC Jeff Hafley's tone turned more cautious Monday (9/21), saying it's "too early to tell/say" whether Douglas plays Miami's Week 3 home opener vs. Kansas City; MRI results still hadn't been disclosed as of that update (NBC Sports).

Fringe top-10 pass rush anchored by Nick Bosa, though the unit ranks closer to the middle of the pack (~20th) in preseason fantasy defense rankings — streaming-caliber if the front seven stays healthy.
Added off waivers with no notable injury or personnel news to report.
Finished outside the top-15 fantasy defenses in each of the past two seasons, but offseason front-seven additions and signings have raised expectations for a step forward in 2026.
Added off waivers with no notable injury or personnel news to report.
Rookie 5th-round pick (No. 161 overall) out of Nebraska in the 2026 draft, where he was Big Ten RB of the Year (1,451 rush yards, 15 total TDs).

Won Kansas City's RB2/backup job in camp after the Chiefs waived veteran Emari Demercado; sits behind clear starter Kenneth Walker III (signed as a free agent from Seattle after being Super Bowl LX MVP). Got 8 carries for 24 yards plus 2 catches for 44 yards in the Week 1 win over Denver.
Pure bench stash for now — standalone value is tied to a Walker injury; not much expected Week 2 volume vs. Indianapolis otherwise.
Stepped into a featured role in New Orleans' Week 1 loss to Detroit with WR2 Jordyn Tyson out on IR (hamstring, expected out at least a month): 7 catches for 69 yards and a TD on 9 targets.

Some caution on the target volume — the Saints ran an unusually high 90 offensive snaps/67 pass attempts in that game (vs. a more typical ~63 snaps), so part of the target spike may be game-script inflated. Still projected as a near-every-down WR while Tyson is out, and a notable Week 2 waiver add.

Backed up the Week 1 breakout with 5 catches for 64 yards on 7 targets in the Saints' 24-17 upset win over Baltimore in Week 2, continuing as New Orleans' clear WR2 opposite Chris Olave while Jordyn Tyson (IR) is out (Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports).
Suffered a severe left knee injury (dislocation with torn ACL/MCL/PCL and patella damage) on Sept 29, 2025 vs. New England, requiring surgery; Miami released him in February 2026 as expected.

Remains an unsigned free agent as of Sept 2026 — has not retired, but has also not signed with any team. Publicly says his recovery "timeline looking real good" but has also said he still has "no power" in the left leg; agent Drew Rosenhaus has indicated doctors want to hold off on a comeback attempt until at least October 2026.
Not rostered by any NFL team — unplayable/bench for now; monitor for a signing or workout announcement.

Played well in the Week 1 Monday-night win over Denver (31-10), helped by a resurgent Chiefs run game controlling the clock; Chris Jones (7 sacks in 2025) remains the defensive anchor as KC rebuilds the unit around him for 2026.
Tougher Week 2 test at home vs. Indianapolis, who bring a strong offensive line and Jonathan Taylor at RB.

Explosive change-of-pace back for the Chargers, but Omarion Hampton is the clear RB1 on the current depth chart; Mitchell has a slight edge over Kimani Vidal for the No. 2 job behind him, per Chargers.com and Yahoo Sports.
Weak as a receiver out of the backfield, which caps his standalone fantasy value to a change-of-pace/big-play role in a Hampton-led committee rather than a real workload threat.

Strong Week 1 vs. Cleveland: 5 sacks on Deshaun Watson, 2 takeaways forced, and held the Browns to 1-for-8 on 3rd down. Analysts are calling the unit borderline top-10 early, with a tougher Week 2 test vs. Cincinnati's offense.
